messages.subject: User defined GWAS model
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am just trying to run the user defined GWAS model, using the following command:
modelGWAS<-userGWAS(SNPcov,estimation="DWLS", model=CommonFactor_userDefined)

For some reason I keep getting this error:
"Error in lavInspect(ReorderModel1, "cor.lv <http://cor.lv>") :
  object 'ReorderModel1' not found"

I don't think it has something to do with model misspecificaton, as I have been able to test the same user defined model including only the output from LD-Score regression, which ran find and showed good model fit statistics:
modelSEM<-usermodel(LDSCoutput, estimation = "DWLS", model = CommonFactor_userDefined, CFIcalc=TRUE)
    chisq df      p_chisq      AIC       CFI      SRMR
df 32.04187 11 0.0007510184 66.04187 0.9599586 0.1131122

Any idea what I am doing wrong here?

As always, many thanks for your help,

Tabea

messages.subject: Re: User defined GWAS model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tabea,

It's strange that you are able to run the model without the individual SNP-effect without issue, but typically I've seen this error pop up when the model is not identified in some way. Is it possible for you to paste the CommonFactor_userDefined model here so I can take a look at the model you are running? I know a specific model identification issues others have run into when running a  common factor model using userGWAS is using unit loading identification for a variable that does not load very highly on the common factor. So in the case of the p-factor model we show on the wiki if I write the code below, then lavaan will fix the loading of anxiety to 1, but since anxiety does not load as highly on the p-factor then the scaling for the other common factor indicators is difficult for lavaan to deal with. On the off chance this is the issue you are running into, this can be solved by listing the variable that loads the highest on the common factor first.

pfactor.model<-'F1=~ANX + SCZ + MDD + PTSD + BIP
F1~SNP'
